title: Emergency recovery loans reduce small-firm exit and bankruptcy after disasters while increasing employment, revenue, and private credit
source_unit: Over 167,000 US firm loan applications spanning about 1,900 disasters, merged to Census records and business credit reports; published causal firm-level research, not a household or customer panel

observations.period: Post-disaster firm follow-up over up to seven years; NBER Working Paper 32326, revised September 2026

denominator.unit: more than 167,000 firm loan applications across approximately 1,900 distinct disasters; paper reports approximate scale

firm_survival.value: Government recovery loans reduce firm exit and bankruptcy
firm_survival.unit: causal firm-level outcome over post-disaster follow-up

employment_and_revenue.value: Recovery loans increase employment and revenue

credit_and_delinquency.value: Loans unlock private credit and reduce delinquency

local_spillover.value: No capital reallocation away from neighboring firms detected; some evidence of positive spillovers on local entry

current_revision_table_4_real_outcomes.value: All firms: exit -13.2 percentage points (SE 4.13 pp), employer-to-nonemployer transition -5.15 pp (SE 2.81 pp), log employment +0.170 (SE 0.0831), and log revenue +0.196 (SE 0.143; not statistically starred). Employer firms: exit -16.9 pp (SE 6.41 pp), deformalization -12.1 pp (SE 5.03 pp), log employment +0.376 (SE 0.183), and log revenue +0.719 (SE 0.254).
current_revision_table_4_real_outcomes.unit: current September 2026 NBER Working Paper 32326 Table 4 IV estimates; outcome-specific panel observation counts and means differ

current_revision_table_5_credit_outcomes.value: Delinquent share of debt -0.339 (SE 0.086), days late on all contracts -34.996 (SE 9.676), bankruptcy -0.038 (SE 0.022), outstanding private debt +17.712 thousand dollars (SE 3.432), private debt paid on time +16.369 thousand dollars (SE 3.350), and number of contracts +0.568 (SE 0.089).
current_revision_table_5_credit_outcomes.unit: current September 2026 NBER Working Paper 32326 Table 5 IV estimates; Experian outcome universes differ

version_labeled_effect_sizes.value: Earlier March 2023 author version remains a historical comparison only: it reported approximately -13 percentage points firm exit, -5 percentage points employer-to-nonemployer transition, +18% employment in the full sample, +45% employment among employer firms, approximately +200% of mean revenue, +$18,000 non-SBA private debt, -3.8 percentage points bankruptcy, and approximately +8 local entrants. These are not silently substituted for the September 2026 table values.
version_labeled_effect_sizes.unit: historical version-specific causal estimates; outcome universes differ

observations.method: Use the NBER authors' merged application, Census, and business-credit design and transcribe current September 2026 NBER Working Paper 32326 Tables 4 and 5 plus Appendix F heterogeneity tables. Preserve causal firm-level scope, outcome-specific panel universes, standard errors, table locations, and the earlier March 2023 version as a separate historical comparison.
observations.uncertainty: The current revision supplies table-level causal estimates but no code, firm identifiers, complete loan-term file, or replication output is retained. Table 4 outcome universes differ; the all-firm revenue estimate is not statistically starred while employer-firm revenue is positive. Firm survival and employment do not establish worker pay, job quality, owner-household recovery, customer prices, service continuity, or local political meaning. Loan access, viability, insurance, collateral, and disaster selection remain design-specific considerations.
observations.subgroup: Firms applying for or receiving government recovery loans after distinct disasters; exact treatment/control and subgroup universes remain in the paper's full design.
observations.counterinterpretation: Keeping firms open may preserve employment and local entry without proving that every borrower was viable, that workers gained security, or that customers retained affordable services. Positive aggregate firm outcomes can coexist with debt obligations, unequal loan access, or shifted costs.

related_sources.claim: Current September 2026 revision; Tables 4 and 5 and Appendices F and I supply the transcribed estimates and heterogeneity/spillover boundaries.
SBA disaster assistance provides the public-program context for repair, working-capital, and recovery financing routes.
The committed source packet records the NBER causal findings, limits, and next test without retaining the working paper or microdata.
The authors' March 2023 version supplies version-labeled effect sizes and design details for the causal firm-level result.

boundary: This record establishes a causal firm-level emergency-liquidity result as summarized by the official NBER paper page, with separately labeled effect-size anchors from an earlier author version. It does not establish worker household security, customer access or prices, owner recovery, local service continuity, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequences.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Current September 2026 NBER PDF read transiently for Tables 4, 5, Appendix F, and Appendix I; PDF not retained; no microdata retained
